newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds came off on Tuesday afternoon after a string of U.S. data was broadly deemed negative and investors were caught by the selling mood, dealers said.
"The U.S. data was rather mixed, but on the whole negative, but we're also seeing a reaction to the bullishness of the past week," one trader said.

The U.S. May consumer price index rose 0.1 percent compared with an expected 0.2 percent, but May industrial output was up 0.4 percent, against 0.2 percent forecast, and May capacity utilisation reached its highest level since September 1995.
Traders said they had seen stronger selling from their customers after a weeklong bull run.
Spreads against bunds were virtually unchanged.
The Amsterdam summit continued after yesterday's stability pact agreement with barely a ripple in the market. Some expressed surprise that the agreement appeared to have had no effect on bonds.
"Obviously it should have been more important yesterday than today. People are saying the market had discounted, but you could see the nervousness, so I can't believe it," one trader said.
Another countered that the market had simply bought on the rumour of agreement and sold the facts.
